input.quote: then neither Ono nor its Affiliates shall Commercialize a Competing Product or grant the right to a licensee or distributor to Commercialize a Competing Product in the Ono Territory prior to the [ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect.
input.rationale: Section 8.2 binds us (Ono and its Affiliates) not to Commercialize "Competing Products" in the Ono Territory. The in-term leg is acceptable: it is reciprocal (Array and its Controlled Affiliates are equally bound), limited to the licensed territory, limited to Commercialization only (Commercialization is defined in Section 1.9 as sales/marketing activities, so our internal development is untouched), and limited to a defined class of compounds other than Binimetinib/Encorafenib rather than "any competing business" — i.e. it sits at or near the fallback. The second leg fails the fallback, however: it is a post-termination restriction of unspecified (redacted) duration running to the "[ * ] anniversary" of termination, which is not capped at 12 months and risks walk-away territory, and neither leg carries an acquisition carve-out (so a Competing Product picked up through M&A would breach). Minimal fix: cap the post-term tail at twelve months and add internal-development and acquisition carve-outs, leaving the reciprocal in-term exclusivity — which is the core of our exclusive Japan licence bargain — intact.

ops.oldText: prior to the [ * ] anniversary of the date such termination takes effect.
ops.newText: prior to the twelve (12) month anniversary of the date such termination takes effect. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, nothing in this Section 8.2 shall restrict Ono or its Affiliates from (A) conducting internal research, development or manufacturing activities with respect to any compound or product, or (B) Commercializing any Competing Product acquired by Ono or its Affiliates in connection with a merger with, or an acquisition of, a Third Party or of the business or assets of a Third Party.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our playbook does not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate, so we have capped the post-termination tail in Section 8.2 at twelve (12) months and carved out our internal development activities and products we acquire through M&A. We can live with the in-term reciprocal exclusivity, but an open-ended post-term restriction is not something we can agree to.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; counterparty is Array BioPharma Inc..

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

input.rationale: Section 8.2 binds us (Ono and its Affiliates) not to Commercialize "Competing Products" in the Ono Territory. The in-term leg is acceptable: it is reciprocal (Array and its Controlled Affiliates are equally bound), limited to the licensed territory, limited to Commercialization only (Commercialization is defined in Section 1.9 as sales/marketing activities, so our internal development is untouched), and limited to a defined class of compounds other than Binimetinib/Encorafenib rather than "any competing business" — i.e. it sits at or near the fallback. The second leg fails the fallback, however: it is a post-termination restriction of unspecified (redacted) duration running to the "[ * ] anniversary" of termination, which is not capped at 12 months and risks walk-away territory, and neither leg carries an acquisition carve-out (so a Competing Product picked up through M&A would breach). Minimal fix: cap the post-term tail at twelve months and add internal-development and acquisition carve-outs, leaving the reciprocal in-term exclusivity — which is the core of our exclusive Japan licence bargain — intact.

payload.text: 18.9 Assignment. This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party to any Third Party without the written consent of the other Party hereto; except either Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's consent to an entity that acquires substantially all of the business or assets of the assigning Party, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise; provided that the acquiring party agrees in a writing delivered to the non-assigning Party to assume all of the rights and obligations of the assigning Party under this Agreement.

In addition, either Party shall have the right to assign this Agreement to an Affiliate, with the prior written consent of the other Party (which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed); provided that the assigning Party guarantees the performance of this Agreement by such Affiliate and such Affiliate agrees in a writing delivered to the non-assigning Party to assume all of the rights and obligations of the assigning Party under this Agreement; and further provided that if the non- assigning Party reasonably believes such assignment could result in material adverse tax consequences to the non-assigning Party, the non-assigning Party shall have no obligation to consent to the proposed assignment. For clarity, any assignment of this Agreement shall be without prejudice to any required review by the relevant competition law authorities. Subject to the foregoing, this Agreement shall inure to the benefit of each Party, its successors and permitted assigns.
Any assignment of this Agreement in contravention of this Section 18.9 shall be null and void.

18.10 Change in Control. In the event of a Change in Control of Array in which the Acquirer is developing or commercializing [ * ] in the Field, any Development and Commercialization of a [ * ], Binimetinib and/or Encorafenib combination by the Parties shall be conducted subject to appropriate firewall procedures to segregate such activities (and the personnel conducting such activities) from the activities performed by or on behalf of Acquirer with respect to [ * ] it is developing or commercializing, to ensure that [ * ] is disclosed to employees of the Acquirer who are developing or commercializing the Acquirer's [ * ].

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; counterparty is Array BioPharma Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; counterparty is Array BioPharma Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 8.2 "Exclusivity of Efforts", p0491–p0492).**

- **In-term leg — acceptable:** reciprocal (Array and its Controlled Affiliates equally bound), confined to the Ono Territory, confined to *Commercialization* only (§1.9 covers sales/marketing, not our internal R&D), and confined to a defined compound class other than Binimetinib/Encorafenib — not "any competing business." That sits at/near the fallback and is the core of our exclusive Japan licence bargain, so we left it alone.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.quote: and (d) any breach of any representations, warranties or covenants by Array in Article 15 above, except to the extent such Third Party Claims result from the gross negligence or willful misconduct of a Ono Indemnitee.
input.rationale: The Agreement has a mutual indemnity architecture (16.1 Ono indemnifies Array; 16.2 Array indemnifies Ono) with standard notice/control/cooperation and settlement-consent procedure in 16.3, so procedure is fine. However, Array's indemnity in 16.2 is limited to Array Territory product activities, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and breaches of Array's Article 15 representations; it contains no limb for third-party claims that the Products or our exercise of the licensed Array Patents/Know-How infringe or misappropriate third-party IP. Article 15 gives no non-infringement warranty and 15.4 expressly disclaims one, and Section 11.4 leaves each party to defend patent Infringement Actions at its own expense, so no route exists to recover from the licensor. Meanwhile our own indemnity in 16.1(a) captures any and all Liabilities from Third Party Claims arising from our Ono Territory commercialization, which on its face includes third-party IP infringement claims against Array. That is the walk-away pattern under this rule (no licensor IP indemnity, with a one-way customer indemnity covering the licensed subject matter) and fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a vendor IP indemnity (usual exclusions/remedies, cap acceptable). The redline adds an IP infringement limb 16.2(e) and a matching carve-out from 16.1(a); the comment flags that usual exclusions (our modifications/combinations) or a cap on this limb are acceptable fallbacks.

proposal.summary: Add Array IP-infringement indemnity limb to Section 16.2 and carve IP claims out of Ono's Section 16.1(a) indemnity
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Array's indemnity in Section 16.2 covers only Array Territory activities, Array-sponsored studies and Article 15 breaches, so no party stands behind third-party IP infringement claims arising from our exercise of the licensed Array Patents and Know-How (and Section 15.4 disclaims any non-infringement warranty), while our Section 16.1(a) indemnity captures every Third Party Claim from our Ono Territory activities, including such IP claims. We have added an IP infringement limb to Array's indemnity and a matching carve-out from ours; we can discuss the usual exclusions (our modifications or combinations) or a cap on this limb as a fallback.

Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

input.rationale: The Agreement has a mutual indemnity architecture (16.1 Ono indemnifies Array; 16.2 Array indemnifies Ono) with standard notice/control/cooperation and settlement-consent procedure in 16.3, so procedure is fine. However, Array's indemnity in 16.2 is limited to Array Territory product activities, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and breaches of Array's Article 15 representations; it contains no limb for third-party claims that the Products or our exercise of the licensed Array Patents/Know-How infringe or misappropriate third-party IP. Article 15 gives no non-infringement warranty and 15.4 expressly disclaims one, and Section 11.4 leaves each party to defend patent Infringement Actions "at its own expense", so no route exists to recover from the licensor. Meanwhile our own indemnity in 16.1(a) captures "any and all Liabilities from any Third Party Claim" arising from our Ono Territory commercialization, which on its face includes third-party IP infringement claims against Array. That is the walk-away pattern under this rule (no licensor IP indemnity, with a one-way customer indemnity covering the licensed subject matter) and fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a vendor IP indemnity (usual exclusions/remedies, cap acceptable). Redline adds an IP infringement limb 16.2(e) and a matching carve-out from 16.1(a); we flagged in the comment that usual exclusions (our modifications/combinations) or a cap on this limb are acceptable fallbacks.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; counterparty is Array BioPharma Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

content.text:
Finding submitted: **deviation** on the indemnity architecture (Art. 16).

- Array's indemnity (16.2) covers only Array Territory product activities, Array-sponsored studies and Article 15 breaches — no third-party IP infringement limb; Article 15 gives no non-infringement warranty and 15.4 disclaims one, and 11.4 leaves each party defending Infringement Actions at its own expense.
- Our indemnity (16.1(a)) sweeps in *all* Third Party Claims from Ono Territory commercialization, including IP claims — the one-way pattern the rule treats as walk-away.
- Redline (validated ok:true): new limb 16.2(e) requiring Array to indemnify for claims that our exercise of the licensed rights or Product activities in the Ono Territory infringe third-party IP, plus a matching carve-out from 16.1(a); fallback (usual exclusions or a cap on that limb) offered in the comment.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

Rule: INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor

Preferred position:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.


Fallback position:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

input.quote: NOTWITHSTANDING THE FOREGOING, NOTHING IN THIS SECTION 16.5 IS INTENDED TO OR SHALL LIMIT OR RESTRICT THE AMOUNTS PAYABLE TO THIRD PARTIES UNDER THE INDEMNITIES PROVIDED PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 10, SECTIONS 16.1 AND 16.2 ABOVE; PROVIDED, FURTHER, THAT THE FOREGOING LIMITATION OF LIABILITY SHALL NOT APPLY IN THE CASE OF GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT.
input.rationale: Section 16.5 (p0727) is a mutual exclusion of special, indirect, punitive, incidental and consequential damages, with carve-outs for the Article 10 / Sections 16.1-16.2 indemnities and for gross negligence and willful misconduct, so the carve-out and mutuality limbs of the fallback are met. However, searches for "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed" and "liability" confirm there is no monetary aggregate cap anywhere in the Agreement (Section 17.3(d) at p0751 only bars the tribunal from awarding punitive or excess damages), so each Party's direct-damages liability is unlimited. The fallback requires a mutual cap of twelve months' fees; the absence of any cap fails that material term, and the exposure is materially adverse to Ono, which carries the commercialization and product-liability indemnity risk for the Ono Territory under Section 16.1. We therefore added a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000, preserving uncapped treatment for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirming Ono's payment obligations are outside the cap.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims to Section 16.5
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 16.5 waives consequential damages but leaves each Party's direct liability entirely uncapped, so we have added a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of twelve (12) months' payments and USD 1,000,000, consistent with our position that liability be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount. Indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Ono's payment obligations are not limited by it; we can accept a straight twelve-month cap without the USD floor if preferred.

ops.text: Cap on Aggregate Liability. Except in respect of Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by Ono to Array under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) one million U.S. dollars (US$1,000,000). "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article X, its indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2, its gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. Ono's obligation to pay amounts due under Article VI and Article VII shall not constitute damages and shall not be subject to the foregoing cap.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; counterparty is Array BioPharma Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims to Section 16.5
input.comment: [Playbook] Section 16.5 waives consequential damages but leaves each Party's direct liability entirely uncapped, so we have added a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of twelve (12) months' payments and USD 1,000,000, consistent with our position that liability be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount. Indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Ono's payment obligations are not limited by it; we can accept a straight twelve-month cap without the USD floor if preferred.

ops.text: Cap on Aggregate Liability. Except in respect of Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the amounts paid or payable by Ono to Array under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) one million U.S. dollars (US$1,000,000). "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article X, its indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2, its gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. Ono's obligation to pay amounts due under Article VI and Article VII shall not constitute damages and shall not be subject to the foregoing cap.

input.rationale: Section 16.5 (p0727) is a mutual exclusion of special, indirect, punitive, incidental and consequential damages, with carve-outs for the Article 10 / Sections 16.1-16.2 indemnities and for gross negligence and willful misconduct, so the carve-out and mutuality limbs of the fallback are met. However, searches for "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed" and "liability" confirm there is no monetary aggregate cap anywhere in the Agreement (Section 17.3(d) at p0751 only bars the tribunal from awarding punitive or excess damages), so each Party's direct-damages liability is unlimited. The fallback requires a mutual cap of twelve months' fees; the absence of any cap fails that material term, and the exposure is materially adverse to Ono, which carries the commercialization and product-liability indemnity risk for the Ono Territory under Section 16.1. We therefore added a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000, preserving uncapped treatment for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirming Ono's payment obligations are outside the cap.

**Finding submitted: deviation (LOL-CAP)**

- **What exists:** Section 16.5 (p0727) is a mutual waiver of special, indirect, punitive, incidental and consequential damages, with carve-outs for the Article 10 / Sections 16.1–16.2 indemnities and for gross negligence and willful misconduct. Mutuality and the fallback carve-out set are satisfied.
- **What fails:** No monetary aggregate cap exists anywhere — confirmed by searches for "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed" and "liability", and by reading Article XVI and Section 17.3(d) (p0751 only restricts the tribunal from awarding punitive/excess damages). Each Party's direct liability is therefore unlimited, which fails the fallback's mutual twelve-month cap and is materially adverse to Ono, who bears the Ono Territory commercialization and product-liability indemnity under Section 16.1.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** inserted a "Cap on Aggregate Liability" sentence after Section 16.5 — mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' payments and USD 1,000,000, with Excluded Claims (confidentiality, indemnities, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) uncapped and Ono's payment obligations expressly outside the cap. Fallback of a straight twelve-month cap offered in the comment.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

content.text: Confirmed: Array (counterparty) is Delaware/Colorado-based; Ono (our client) is Osaka-based. This matters for the seat analysis.

input.quote: The seat of the arbitration shall be in Osaka, Japan, if it is demanded by Array, and in New York, NY, USA, if it is demanded by Ono, with hearings to held in the same location.
input.rationale: Governing law meets the preferred position exactly: Section 18.3 (p0765) provides that the Agreement "shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, United States," with CISG excluded. On forum, Section 17.3 (p0747-p0748) provides mandatory ICC arbitration before three arbitrators rather than the preferred New York courts, but this does not reach walk-away territory. Walk-away is defined as the vendor's home jurisdiction with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad. Here neither seat option is Array's home jurisdiction (Array is a Delaware company based in Boulder, Colorado): the seat is New York, NY when Ono demands arbitration — a fully accepted venue — and Osaka, Japan when Array demands, which is our own client's home city (Ono is organized under the laws of Japan with its principal place of business in Osaka). The demand-based election is reciprocal and, in the only case where the seat falls outside the accepted list, it lands on our home turf, so that limb benefits our party and we do not flag it. Court access is also preserved: each Party retains the right to apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for provisional and conservatory relief (p0757), and either Party may seek recognition and enforcement of any award before any competent court (p0751). Noted in passing but not flagged as deviations: the forum is arbitration rather than courts, the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions are disapplied, and Section 18.3 governing law is carved out from procedural issues (p0749) — sub-elements short of preferred wording that do not disadvantage us given the New York substantive law and preserved court remedies.

content.text: Confirmed: Array (counterparty) is Delaware/Colorado-based; Ono (our client) is Osaka-based. This matters for the seat analysis.

input.quote: The seat of the arbitration shall be in Osaka, Japan, if it is demanded by Array, and in New York, NY, USA, if it is demanded by Ono, with hearings to held in the same location.
input.rationale: Governing law meets the preferred position exactly: Section 18.3 (p0765) provides that the Agreement "shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, United States," with CISG excluded. On forum, Section 17.3 (p0747-p0748) provides mandatory ICC arbitration before three arbitrators rather than the preferred New York courts, but this does not reach walk-away territory. Walk-away is defined as the vendor's home jurisdiction with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad. Here neither seat option is Array's home jurisdiction (Array is a Delaware company based in Boulder, Colorado): the seat is New York, NY when Ono demands arbitration — a fully accepted venue — and Osaka, Japan when Array demands, which is our own client's home city (Ono is organized under the laws of Japan with its principal place of business in Osaka). The demand-based election is reciprocal and, in the only case where the seat falls outside the accepted list, it lands on our home turf, so that limb benefits our party and we do not flag it. Court access is also preserved: each Party retains the right to apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for provisional and conservatory relief (p0757), and either Party may seek recognition and enforcement of any award before any competent court (p0751). Noted in passing but not flagged as deviations: the forum is arbitration rather than courts, the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions are disapplied, and Section 18.3 governing law is carved out from procedural issues (p0749) — sub-elements short of preferred wording that do not disadvantage us given the New York substantive law and preserved court remedies.

input.quote: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Commencing on the later of (i) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product in the Ono Territory, or (ii) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Encorafenib Product in the Ono Territory, Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, for any reasons by giving [ * ] advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.
input.rationale: Direction is favourable on the Vendor side: Array has no termination-for-convenience right at all (Sections 13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy and 8.2 exclusivity breach are its only routes), which meets the preferred position. The failure is on our side. The term under Section 13.1 runs product-by-product until expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term, i.e. many years, yet our at-will exit under 13.2 does not become available until the later of two redacted periods measured from First Commercial Sale of both the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products. Through the whole development and pre-launch phase — where our spend and risk are greatest — we have no convenience right (only 13.5 Safety/Efficacy and 13.3 breach), which is the walk-away case of "no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term". The notice period is also redacted, so the fallback 60–90 day band cannot be verified. Redline removes the First Commercial Sale gate and fixes notice at ninety (90) days, which is longer than our preferred thirty (30) days but proportionate given the extensive Article 14 wind-down obligations. Noted but not separately flagged: on a 13.2 exit we bear the transition and ongoing Clinical Study costs (p0647, p0656) and are subject to a post-termination Competing Product restriction (p0492) — these are the real price of convenience and belong to the exclusivity/exit-cost rules rather than a second redline here.

proposal.summary: Remove the First Commercial Sale time-gate on Ono's Section 13.2 at-will termination right and fix the notice period at 90 days
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13.2 only lets us exit at will after First Commercial Sale of both Products, so we are locked into a multi-year term through the entire development phase; our playbook requires a customer convenience right exercisable throughout the term. We have made the right available at any time on ninety (90) days' notice (longer than our usual thirty (30) days) to accommodate the Article 14 wind-down machinery.

Parties: we represent Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; counterparty is Array BioPharma Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

input.quote: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Commencing on the later of (i) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product in the Ono Territory, or (ii) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Encorafenib Product in the Ono Territory, Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, for any reasons by giving [ * ] advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.
input.rationale: Direction is favourable on the Vendor side: Array has no termination-for-convenience right at all (Sections 13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy and 8.2 exclusivity breach are its only routes), which meets the preferred position. The failure is on our side. The term under Section 13.1 runs product-by-product until expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term, i.e. many years, yet our at-will exit under 13.2 does not become available until the later of two redacted periods measured from First Commercial Sale of both the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products. Through the whole development and pre-launch phase — where our spend and risk are greatest — we have no convenience right (only 13.5 Safety/Efficacy and 13.3 breach), which is the walk-away case of "no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term". The notice period is also redacted, so the fallback 60–90 day band cannot be verified. Redline removes the First Commercial Sale gate and fixes notice at ninety (90) days, which is longer than our preferred thirty (30) days but proportionate given the extensive Article 14 wind-down obligations. Noted but not separately flagged: on a 13.2 exit we bear the transition and ongoing Clinical Study costs (p0647, p0656) and are subject to a post-termination Competing Product restriction (p0492) — these are the real price of convenience and belong to the exclusivity/exit-cost rules rather than a second redline here.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

Use the document tools for any needed source inspection. Call propose_redline until it returns ok:true, then submit exactly once with the locked status and stop.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Section 18.9 already delivers the substance of this rule, symmetrically:

- **Successor carve-out present.** Either Party — including Ono — may assign **without** the other's consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of its business or assets by merger, acquisition or otherwise, subject only to a written assumption. That is better than the fallback (which would only require notice) and matches the preferred position's M&A carve-out.
- **Consent standard acceptable.** Affiliate assignments require prior written consent "which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed" — the fallback standard, and it binds Array equally.
- **No vendor exit on our change of control.** The only change-of-control triggers in the document run against *Array*, not Ono: Section 18.10 (p0788) imposes firewall obligations on Array's acquirer, and Section 4.5(b) (p0322) lapses on an Array Change in Control. Nothing gives Array a termination or re-pricing right if Ono is acquired, so the walk-away scenario is absent.

Noted in the rationale but deliberately **not** flagged as deviations (minor sub-elements under the classification rules):

- Preferred wording would permit Affiliate assignment with no consent at all; here consent is needed, albeit on a reasonableness standard.
- The proviso permitting refusal of consent where the non-assigning Party reasonably believes an Affiliate assignment could cause it material adverse tax consequences is narrow and reciprocal.
- Separately, p0322 allows Array's Section 4.5(b) restrictions to terminate on Array's own Change in Control. That is a non-compete/exclusivity concern rather than an assignment failure, so it belongs to another rule and is not double-flagged here.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

**Governing law (Section 18.3, p0765):** Meets the **preferred** position exactly — laws of the State of New York, with CISG expressly excluded.

**Forum (Section 17.3, p0747–p0748):** Mandatory three-arbitrator ICC arbitration rather than the preferred New York courts. I assessed this against the walk-away trigger and it does not fail:

- The walk-away is *the vendor's home jurisdiction with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad*. Neither seat option here is Array's home jurisdiction — Array is a Delaware company headquartered in Boulder, Colorado (p0004).
- Seat is **New York, NY** when Ono demands — a fully accepted venue.
- Seat is **Osaka, Japan** only when Array demands — and Osaka is *our client's own principal place of business*. The single limb falling outside the accepted list lands on our home turf, so it benefits our party and should not be flagged.
- The election is reciprocal and structured so the claimant bears the less convenient seat, not so that one party gets a systematic home-forum advantage.

**Court access preserved:** Either Party may apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for provisional/conservatory relief, including injunctions and TROs, before or after tribunal constitution (p0757), and may seek recognition and enforcement of any award before any competent court (p0751).

**Noted in the rationale but not flagged** (sub-elements short of preferred wording, none adverse to us): arbitration rather than courts as the primary forum; disapplication of the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions; and the carve-out of Section 18.3 governing law from procedural and evidentiary issues (p0749), which preserves privilege protections for both Parties.

A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. - LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.

Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras.
