system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.rationale: Article XIV is a detailed wind-down regime, but every operative transition and return obligation runs against us: we must transition studies, keep distributing, assign Regulatory Filings and hand over Data and Ono Know-How (p0659), and return or destroy Array's Materials and Confidential Information (p0662). The only mutual language is the general cooperation covenant in Section 14.2(a)(iv) (p0660), which merely transitions the Product back to Array. Nothing obliges Array to give us transition assistance or to return, delete and certify deletion of our Data and Confidential Information, so the rule's clause is absent. We therefore insert a reciprocal Section 14.2(a)(x) at the preferred level: up to six (6) months' assistance at Array's then-current rates, return of our Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days after expiry or termination, and deletion with written certification thereafter.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule: TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return

Preferred position:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.


Fallback position:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
with Ono's obligations during the Wind Down Period. In addition, Ono shall promptly provide to Array a copy of all Data and Ono Know-How pertaining to the Product in the Ono Territory to the extent not previously provided to Array and Array shall have a fully-paid-up right to use and disclose all Data and Ono Know-How pertaining to the Product following termination of this Agreement, except in case of termination by Ono pursuant to Section 13.3 or 13.4, in which case the Section 14.2(a)(ix) shall apply. In addition, all such Data and Ono Know-How, to the extent solely related to the Product, shall be deemed Confidential Information of Array and not Confidential Information of Ono (and will not be subject to the exclusions under Sections 10.1(a) or (e) above).
(iv) Transition. Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other and/or its designee to effect a smooth and orderly transition in the Development, sale and ongoing marketing, promotion and commercialization of the Product in the Ono Territory during the Wind-down Period and to conduct in an expeditious manner any activities to be conducted under this Section 14.2. Without limiting the foregoing, Ono shall, upon written request from Array, provide Array copies of customer lists, customer data and other customer information relating to the Product in the Ono Territory (except as prevented by the applicable Laws and regulations relating to the protection of personal information), which Array shall have the right to use and disclose. For clarity, "customers" means prescribers and individuals and entities with the ability to influence use of the Product (e.g. individuals responsible for hospital formularies and/or making purchasing decisions on behalf of the hospital) that are called on by Ono representatives when detailing the Product.
(vi) Return of Materials. Within ninety (90) days after the end of the Wind-down Period, upon request by Array, Ono shall either deliver to Array or destroy all tangible items comprising, bearing or containing trademarks of Array (including the Product Trademarks), trade names, patents, copyrights, designs, drawings, formulas or other Data, photographs, samples, literature, sales and promotional aids ("Product Materials") and Confidential Information of Array, that is in Ono's possession, subject to Ono's right to keep one (1) copy for archiving purposes. Effective upon the end of the Wind-down Period, Ono shall cease to use all trademarks and trade names of Array (including the Product Trademarks) in the Ono Territory, and all rights granted to Ono hereunder with respect to the Product in the Ono Territory shall terminate.
(ix) Following a termination by Ono pursuant to Section 13.3 or 13.4, in the event that Array wishes to have Ono: (A) assign to Array the Regulatory Filings for the Product in the Ono Territory and provide to Array a copy of all Data and Ono Know-How pertaining to the Product as described in 14.2(a)(iii) above, and/or (B) grant to Array a non-exclusive license under any Improvements, and/or under any other Patents owned or Controlled by Ono related to any Product(s) (including without limitation, Ono's interest in any Joint Patents) as described in 14.2(a)(v) above, Array shall so notify Ono and Ono shall make such rights for consideration consistent with then-prevailing market conditions, on customary terms and conditions to be negotiated in good faith. In the event that the Parties cannot finalize such an agreement within sixty (60) days of commencing negotiations with respect thereto, the agreement shall be referred for resolution pursuant to Section 17.3 applied mutatis mutandis to such agreement.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-indemn-dead841d","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS","rationale":"Array's indemnity in Section 16.2 is limited to Array Territory product activities, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and breaches of Array's Article 15 representations; it contains no limb for third-party claims that the Products or our exercise of the licensed Array Patents/Know-How infringe or misappropriate third-party IP (and Section 15.4 disclaims any non-infringement warranty), while our Section 16.1(a) indemnity covers all Third Party Claims from our Ono Territory activities. That fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a licensor IP indemnity. We take the fallback position: a single concise IP indemnity limb with the usual exclusions (our modifications, combinations, specifications), the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder and a 3x annual fees super-cap, which is the least intrusive cure and leaves the existing mutual architecture and Section 16.3 procedure untouched.","proposal":"Insert Array IP-infringement indemnity (usual exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, 3x annual fees super-cap) after Section 16.2","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-ip-b2c56708","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"PATENT PROSECUTION AND ENFORCEMENT","rationale":"The IP allocation works in our favour and no Ono IP or data is assigned to Array during the term. Section 11.1(a) gives Ono outright ownership of everything made solely by Ono personnel (Array's ownership of its own compound IP under 11.1(b) is the acceptable "vendor keeps its platform" position), Section 4.6(c) (p0329) confirms Ono owns its INDs and Marketing Approvals in the Ono Territory, Section 2.7 preserves each Party's retained rights, and Section 13.1 converts our Article II licences into perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, royalty-free, sublicensable licences on expiry — which independently satisfies the fallback licence-back requirement. The outbound Grant-Back in Section 2.6 is a non-exclusive, subject-to-our-exclusivity licence of Improvements and our Joint IP interest, not an assignment, so it is not walk-away territory. Two points sit at the fallback rather than the preferred position and are noted rather than redlined: (i) Section 11.1(c) does create joint ownership of jointly-made IP, and 11.1(d) limits each Party to internal practice and requires the other Party's consent to enforce, license or assign — but the restriction is reciprocal and expressly disapplied "to the extent any jointly-owned inventions or intellectual property are included in subject matter licensed by one Party to the other", and our Section 2.1(a)-(c) licences cover Array's interests in the Joint Patents and Joint Know-How for Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products throughout the Ono Territory, so we retain a workable right to exploit joint IP across our whole commercial field; (ii) Sections 14.2(a)(iii) and (vii) require assignment of Product-specific Regulatory Filings and Product Trademarks on termination, but that is ordinary reversion of a licensed product (our corporate names are carved out) and, where we terminate for Array's material breach or insolvency under 13.3/13.4, Section 14.2(a)(ix) requires Array to pay market-rate consideration for those rights instead. No redline warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-50655a50","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Section 18.9 is fully mutual and contains the M&A/successor carve-out: either Party (including Ono) may assign without the other's consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of its business or assets by merger, acquisition or otherwise, subject only to an assumption writing. Other assignments require consent, and Affiliate assignments are permitted with consent that "shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed" — i.e., the rule's fallback consent standard, applied symmetrically to Array as well as to us. There is no Array right to terminate, re-price or otherwise exit on an Ono change of control: the only change-of-control provisions in the document (Section 18.10 and Section 4.5(b) at p0322) are triggered by a Change in Control of Array, not of Ono, and Section 18.10 imposes firewall obligations on Array's acquirer rather than granting any exit right. This sits at (and on the successor carve-out above) the fallback, so no redline. Noted but not flagged as deviations: the preferred position would allow Affiliate assignment without consent, and the proviso letting the non-assigning Party refuse consent where it reasonably believes an Affiliate assignment could cause it material adverse tax consequences is a narrow, reciprocal qualifier on a minor sub-element. We would also observe commercially (not as an assignment issue) that p0322 lets Array's Section 4.5(b) restrictions lapse on Array's own Change in Control, which is a separate non-compete point rather than a breach of this rule.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-69a7ec37","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY","rationale":"No sole-supplier or requirements-purchase obligation is imposed on us. Article IX frames supply entirely as our option: Section 9.4(a) (p0508) gives Ono the right but not the obligation to Manufacture or engage its own Subcontractor, with Know-How transfer and step-in rights; Section 9.4(b) (p0509) says Ono shall have the right to obtain commercial requirements from Array, with a Supply Agreement entered into only upon Ono's request. Section 9.1(a) (p0495) obliges Array to supply or secure supply of our requirements with no reciprocal exclusive-purchase commitment from us, and Section 9.5 (p0516) passes through the benefit of Array's Third Party supplier arrangements. Our freedom to second-source is fully preserved, meeting the preferred position. The only exclusivity binding us is Section 8.2 (p0491), a reciprocal field non-compete rather than exclusive dealing: mutual (Array and its Controlled Affiliates equally bound), limited to two defined Competing Product categories, limited to the Ono Territory, time-limited to a defined date, and the quid pro quo for the exclusive licences granted to us under Sections 2.1(a) and 2.1(c) (p0162, p0164), which benefit us and are not flagged. That covenant sits at or above the fallback; we note only that it does not expressly release us if Array itself commercialises a Competing Product (it instead ends the royalty period), a minor sub-element rather than a material failure. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-451be3b8","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ XIV EFFECT OF TERMINATION","rationale":"The Agreement meets the preferred position: there are no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Ono (our party). The only liquidated damages clause, Section 14.3 (p0668/p0671), runs entirely in our favour — it is triggered by Array's conduct (including intentional concealment or falsification of safety/efficacy data) and gives Ono the election to continue the Agreement with (A) relief from its own due diligence obligations and (B) a reduction in the otherwise applicable royalty rate as the liquidated amount. Per the playbook, LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant and we do not flag a clause that benefits us.

I checked the other candidates and Article VII for any Customer-payable penalty and found none: (i) p0430 is a royalty true-up/reconciliation — a shortfall of royalties actually owed on Net Sales, not a penalty or fixed damages amount; (ii) Section 7.1 (p0463) is mutual, reciprocal late-payment interest at LIBOR plus a margin on sums actually overdue, payable by whichever Party is delinquent, which is compensatory interest rather than liquidated damages; (iii) there is no early-termination fee, minimum annual royalty, forfeiture or minimum-payment-on-termination anywhere in the document (searches for "penalty", "termination fee", "minimum", "forfeit" and "minimum annual royalty" returned nothing relevant). Section 14.5 confirms only milestone and royalty payments already accrued survive termination.

One note for the record, not a deviation under this rule: Sections 14.2(a)(i) and 14.2(a)(iii) allocate the actual costs of wind-down transfers and ongoing Clinical Studies to Ono where Ono terminates for convenience under Section 13.2 or Array terminates for cause. These are reimbursements of genuine costs incurred, uncapped but not a stipulated sum, so they are cost allocation rather than a liquidated damages or penalty mechanic and fall outside this rule. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-3fedd023","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ II GRANT OF LICENSE","rationale":"The grant package meets the preferred position on every material term. Array grants Ono exclusive Development and Commercialization licences (2.1(a), (c)) and a worldwide non-exclusive Manufacturing licence (2.1(b)), and our Affiliates are covered as of right — Section 2.2(a) permits sublicensing to Affiliates without consent, and 2.1(b) is expressly sublicensable to Affiliates — which is better than the fallback's "affiliates on written notice." Contractors acting on our behalf are covered: 2.1(b) expressly allows extension to Third Party manufacturers "for Manufacturing the Products on Ono's behalf," and the Subcontractor definition (1.57) and Articles IV/IX contemplate performance of activities through Subcontractors. Nothing is revocable at Array's discretion: Array can terminate only for uncured material breach (13.3, 90/60-day cure) or bankruptcy (13.4), while at-will termination rights sit with us (13.2, 13.5), and on expiry the Section 2.1 licences become "fully paid-up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty free licenses, with sublicensing rights" (13.1). Successor transfer is satisfied by Section 18.9, which permits assignment without consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of the business or assets by merger or acquisition, with the Agreement inuring to successors and permitted assigns. Two sub-elements fall short of ideal but are not material deviations and are noted only: engaging a Third Party as Sublicensee or distributor of the Product needs Array's prior written consent, and the licences exclude any right to modify Binimetinib or Encorafenib (2.1(d)) — ordinary field limits in a pharma collaboration rather than an exclusion of affiliates/contractors with no path to add them. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-6f742de9","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Governing law meets the preferred position exactly: Section 18.3 (p0765) provides that the Agreement "shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, United States," with CISG excluded. On forum, Section 17.3 (p0747-p0748) provides mandatory ICC arbitration before three arbitrators rather than the preferred New York courts, but this does not reach walk-away territory. Walk-away is defined as the vendor's home jurisdiction with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad. Here neither seat option is Array's home jurisdiction (Array is a Delaware company based in Boulder, Colorado): the seat is New York, NY when Ono demands arbitration — a fully accepted venue — and Osaka, Japan when Array demands, which is our own client's home city (Ono is organized under the laws of Japan with its principal place of business in Osaka). The demand-based election is reciprocal and, in the only case where the seat falls outside the accepted list, it lands on our home turf, so that limb benefits our party and we do not flag it. Court access is also preserved: each Party retains the right to apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for provisional and conservatory relief (p0757), and either Party may seek recognition and enforcement of any award before any competent court (p0751). Noted in passing but not flagged as deviations: the forum is arbitration rather than courts, the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions are disapplied, and Section 18.3 governing law is carved out from procedural issues (p0749) — sub-elements short of preferred wording that do not disadvantage us given the New York substantive law and preserved court remedies.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-ae0d5337","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY","rationale":"Searches across the standard MFN phrasings ("most favored/favoured nation", "no less favorable", "as favorable", "more favorable", "better terms", "best price", "first refusal", "match") return no clause obliging Ono to extend Array terms no less favourable than those given to any third party, and no obligation to match third-party offers. The two closest analogues both run in our favour: p0502 protects Ono by barring Array from forcing direct Subcontractor orders unless the terms are as favorable to Ono as those the Subcontractors extend to Array, and p0190 requires Array to use Diligent Efforts to pass through Third Party Partner data, rights of reference and improvements to Ono without charge. The only other "favorable" reference (p0476) is a routine withholding-tax rate provision, not an MFN. This meets the preferred position — no MFN obligation burdens the Customer — so no redline is warranted; per the rule, MFN benefits flowing to us are welcome and are not flagged.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-17d9b54b","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, minimum royalty or volume commitment on us. Article IX runs in our favour: Array must supply our requirements of Materials (p0495, p0510) and procure clinical Materials as we reasonably request at cost (p0501), while we hold rights, not obligations — the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture or source Materials ourselves (p0508) and the right (not a duty) to obtain commercial requirements from Array (p0509). Forecasting and ordering mechanics are deferred to the future clinical and commercial Supply Agreements, so no binding volume is created here; we should ensure those agreements likewise avoid non-cancellable minimums when negotiated. The only "shortfall" reference (p0430) is a year-end royalty true-up reconciliation, not a purchase minimum. This meets the preferred position (fees for ordered supply only), so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-fb8f9eaa","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VIII CERTAIN COVENANTS","rationale":"Searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce", "employee" and "personnel" returned no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere in the Agreement, and a full read of Article VIII (Certain Covenants) confirms it contains only diligence, conflicts-of-interest and product exclusivity covenants (Section 8.2 restricts Commercializing Competing Products, not hiring personnel). Article XVIII (General Provisions) likewise contains no such covenant. This matches our preferred position of no non-solicit binding Ono as Customer, so no redline is warranted; the absence of any restriction on hiring Array personnel is favourable to us and should not be raised.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-d037a7fa","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"The auto-renewal mechanics this rule targets are not used in this agreement. Section 13.1 sets a single, self-liquidating term running from the Effective Date until expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term on a Product-by-Product/country-by-country basis; there is no automatic renewal, no successive renewal term, and therefore no non-renewal notice window or renewal price uplift to compute (a document-wide search for "renew"/renewal-term language returns only patent-term renewals and Section 14.4, which expressly disclaims any renewal or extension by conduct). The structure is better than the preferred position for us: on expiry the Section 2.1 licences convert to perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, royalty-free licences to Ono, and Section 13.2 gives Ono (not Array) a without-cause termination right on advance notice. No renewal exit or pricing exposure arises, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-2be70aae","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ XIV EFFECT OF TERMINATION","rationale":"Article XIV is a detailed wind-down regime, but every operative transition and return obligation runs against us: we must transition studies, keep distributing, assign Regulatory Filings and hand over Data and Ono Know-How (p0659), and return or destroy Array's Materials and Confidential Information (p0662). The only mutual language is the general cooperation covenant in Section 14.2(a)(iv) (p0660), which merely transitions the Product back to Array. Nothing obliges Array to give us transition assistance or to return, delete and certify deletion of our Data and Confidential Information, so the rule's clause is absent. We therefore insert a reciprocal Section 14.2(a)(x) at the preferred level: up to six (6) months' assistance at Array's then-current rates, return of our Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days after expiry or termination, and deletion with written certification thereafter.","proposal":"Insert reciprocal Array transition-assistance and Customer Data return/deletion as new Section 14.2(a)(x)","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-audit-28d85557","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ IV DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATORY ACTIVITIES","rationale":"Two audit regimes bind us. Section 7.4 (p0481-p0482) is acceptable: inspections no more than once each Calendar Year, one inspection per quarter's records, by an independent accounting firm reasonably acceptable to Ono under a confidentiality agreement, at Array's expense unless underpayment exceeds a stated (redacted) threshold — at or near the preferred position. Section 4.9(a) (p0359), however, gives Array itself an unlimited-frequency right to enter Ono's and its Affiliates' facilities on merely "reasonable advance notice", with no independent auditor, no confidentiality undertaking, no cost allocation and no limit on access. That falls below the fallback and into walk-away territory, so we have made minimal edits requiring an independent auditor, one inspection per Calendar Year on 30 days' prior written notice at Array's cost unless an underpayment exceeding 5% is established, with a confidentiality undertaking, off-site inspection where possible and no direct access to Ono's systems; on-site access is otherwise retained given the GxP context.","proposal":"Limit Section 4.9(a) inspections to an independent auditor, once per Calendar Year on 30 days' written notice at Array's cost, off-site where possible and with no direct systems access.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-insurance-4fd711e3","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"No insurance covenant exists anywhere in the Agreement: searches for "insurance"/"insur*"/"coverage" return only Net Sales deduction items (p0101, p0102) and "insurrection" in force majeure (p0763). Article 16 (p0715–p0727) provides reciprocal indemnities, a damages disclaimer and recall allocation, and Article 18 General Provisions (p0759–p0796) contains no insurance requirement, so the indemnities from Array — who manufactures and supplies Product (Article IX), sponsors Clinical Studies and receives our Confidential Information — are unbacked by any coverage requirement. This falls below even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Array / Ono Collaboration and Licence Agreement (CONFIDENTIAL)

**Prepared for:** Client (Ono, as Customer/Licensee)  
**Prepared by:** In-house counsel  
**Subject:** Playbook review findings and proposed redlines

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is broadly favourable to us: the licence grant, IP ownership and licence-back, assignment/change of control, governing law, exclusivity and supply, minimum commitments, MFN, non-solicitation, liquidated damages and renewal all sit at or above our preferred or fallback positions and require no redline. In several places the terms run affirmatively in our favour (perpetual, royalty-free licences on expiry under Section 13.1; liquidated damages payable only by Array under Section 14.3; no minimum purchase or take-or-pay obligation on us), and we do not raise those.

Seven items require action. Two are critical or structural: (i) Array gives **no IP-infringement indemnity** — its Section 16.2 indemnity is confined to Array Territory activities, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and Article 15 breaches, while Section 15.4 disclaims any non-infringement warranty and our Section 16.1(a) indemnity is broad; and (ii) there is **no post-termination transition assistance or return/deletion of our Data** running against Array, whereas Article XIV imposes extensive wind-down duties on us. In addition, there is **no monetary liability cap anywhere in the Agreement** (Section 16.5 excludes only indirect damages), **no forward-looking performance warranty** (Article 15 is Effective Date representations only), **no insurance covenant** at all, an **unlimited-frequency Array inspection right** over our facilities in Section 4.9(a), a **post-termination non-compete** running to a redacted anniversary rather than 12 months, and our **at-will termination right in Section 13.2 gated** behind redacted periods measured from First Commercial Sale of both Products.

Two of these — the Section 4.9(a) audit right and the absence of any convenience exit during a multi-year term — are identified in the playbook as walk-away territory. Five of the proposed redlines did not clear automated verification and require manual drafting before the markup is issued.

---

## 2. Findings

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS (§16.2; cf. §15.4, §16.1(a), §16.3) | No limb for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims; fails fallback requiring at minimum a licensor IP indemnity. Cure at fallback: one concise IP indemnity limb, usual exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund ladder, 3x annual fees super-cap. | Repaired |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | PATENT PROSECUTION AND ENFORCEMENT (§11.1; §§2.6, 2.7, 4.6(c), 13.1, 14.2(a)) | Allocation favours us; §13.1 licence conversion independently satisfies the fallback licence-back. Joint IP consent mechanic (§11.1(c)–(d)) and termination assignments (§14.2(a)(iii), (vii)) sit at the fallback and are noted only. | — |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS (§18.9; cf. §18.10, §4.5(b)) | Fully mutual with M&A/successor carve-out; Affiliate consent not to be unreasonably withheld (fallback standard). No Array exit on an Ono change of control. | — |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY (§§9.1(a), 9.4(a)–(b), 9.5; cf. §8.2) | No sole-supplier or requirements obligation; supply is our option. §8.2 is a reciprocal, territory- and field-limited non-compete, at or above fallback. | — |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § XIV EFFECT OF TERMINATION (§14.3; cf. §§7.1, 14.5) | Only LD clause runs in our favour. §7.1 is reciprocal late-payment interest; no termination fee or minimum. §14.2(a)(i)/(iii) cost allocation noted, outside this rule. | — |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § II GRANT OF LICENSE (§§2.1(a)–(d), 2.2(a); cf. §§13.1–13.5, 18.9) | Meets preferred position; Affiliates covered as of right, contractors permitted, no revocability at Array's discretion. Sublicensee/distributor consent and no-modification limit noted only. | — |
| 7 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS (§18.3; §17.3) | New York law meets preferred position; ICC arbitration seated in New York or Osaka, neither being Array's home jurisdiction. Court access for provisional relief and enforcement preserved. | — |
| 8 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY | No MFN binding us; the closest analogues run in our favour. | — |
| 9 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY | No minimum, take-or-pay or volume commitment; we hold rights, not obligations. Volume mechanics deferred to future Supply Agreements. | — |
| 10 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § VIII CERTAIN COVENANTS | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere; matches preferred position. | — |
| 11 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | TERM AND TERMINATION (§13.1; cf. §§13.2, 14.4) | Single self-liquidating term; no auto-renewal, notice window or uplift. Better than preferred for us. | — |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § XIV EFFECT OF TERMINATION (§14.2(a); cf. §14.2(a)(iv)) | All transition and return obligations run against us. Insert reciprocal §14.2(a)(x): up to 6 months' assistance at Array's then-current rates, return of our Data in machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. | Repaired |
| 13 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § IV DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATORY ACTIVITIES (§4.9(a); cf. §7.4) | §7.4 is acceptable. §4.9(a) gives Array itself unlimited-frequency facility access on "reasonable advance notice" with no independent auditor, confidentiality undertaking or cost allocation. | **Fail — manual drafting** |
| 14 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | GENERAL PROVISIONS (Art. 18; cf. Art. 16) | No insurance covenant anywhere; Array's indemnities are unbacked. Below the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). Insert §18.15 at preferred limits; Array may evidence equivalent cover under the Quality/Supply Agreements. | Pass |
| 15 | Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS (§16.5; cf. §17.3(d)) | Mutual indirect-damages exclusion only; no monetary aggregate cap, so direct-damages liability is unlimited. Fails the fallback's mutual 12-month cap and is materially adverse given our Ono Territory indemnity exposure. | **Fail — manual drafting** |
| 16 | Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | § VIII CERTAIN COVENANTS (§8.2) | In-term leg acceptable at fallback (reciprocal, territory- and Commercialization-limited). Post-termination leg runs to a redacted anniversary, uncapped at 12 months, with no internal-development or M&A carve-outs. | **Fail — manual drafting** |
| 17 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation (walk-away)** | TERM AND TERMINATION (§§13.1–13.2; cf. §§13.3, 13.4, 8.2) | Multi-year term, but our at-will exit is gated on redacted periods from First Commercial Sale of both Products, with a redacted notice period — no convenience right through development and pre-launch. Array-side element already met. | **Fail — manual drafting** |
| 18 | Low | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES AND COVENANTS (Art. 15; §15.4) | Effective Date representations plus mutual disclaimer only; no forward-looking performance warranty and no repair/replacement/refund remedy. Conformance deferred to unexecuted supply agreements. §15.4 is acceptable as mutual and prefaced "Except as otherwise expressly set forth in this Agreement". | **Fail — manual drafting** |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

Two findings reach walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Section 4.9(a) — Array's inspection right over our facilities (AUDIT).** Unlimited frequency, on merely "reasonable advance notice", with no independent auditor, no confidentiality undertaking, no cost allocation and no limit on access. Our minimum landing zone: independent auditor; one inspection per Calendar Year on 30 days' prior written notice; at Array's cost unless an underpayment exceeding 5% is established; confidentiality undertaking; off-site inspection where possible; no direct access to our systems. We retain on-site access otherwise, given the GxP context.
2. **Section 13.2 — absence of any convenience exit for us during the development and pre-launch phase (T4C).** A multi-year term under Section 13.1 with no Customer convenience right is the playbook's walk-away case. Our landing zone: remove the First Commercial Sale gate, 30 days' written notice, and pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

We would also treat the **missing Array IP-infringement indemnity (item 1)** and the **absence of any liability cap (item 15)** as high-priority asks; both fail the fallback on a material term, and together they leave us with unlimited direct-damages exposure and no recourse for third-party IP claims on the licensed Array Patents and Know-How.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Manual drafting required.** Five proposed redlines did not clear verification and must be drafted and re-verified before the markup issues: AUDIT (§4.9(a)), LOL-CAP (new §16.6), NONCOMPETE (§8.2), T4C (§13.2) and WARRANTY (new §15.5).
2. **Confirm the two repaired redlines** — the Array IP indemnity limb after §16.2 and the reciprocal transition/data-return provision at §14.2(a)(x) — read cleanly against the existing mutual indemnity architecture and the §16.3 procedure, which we have left untouched.
3. **Issue the insurance insert (§18.15)** as drafted, and ask Array whether equivalent coverage is carried under the Quality/Supply Agreements; if so, we can accept certificates in lieu.
4. **Obtain the redacted figures** underpinning items 16 and 17 (the post-termination anniversary in §8.2; the First Commercial Sale periods and notice period in §13.2) and the §7.4 underpayment threshold, so we can confirm whether any of these in fact sit at the fallback.
5. **Flag for the deal team, not as a legal issue:** (a) the future clinical and commercial Supply Agreements must likewise avoid non-cancellable minimums (item 9); and (b) Array's §4.5(b) restrictions lapse on Array's own Change in Control, which is a commercial non-compete point rather than an assignment breach (item 3).
6. **Sequence the negotiation** around the two walk-away items plus the indemnity and liability cap; the remaining compliant items require no discussion and should not be reopened."}
